args.author: agent:long-lived-fly
args.body: the front door now ROUTES the requirement instead of dropping it: 0 requirement(s) for physics_check, 1 for performance_check, 0 that no layer takes. "lives longer" goes to performance_check { kind: "lifespan" }, and the quantities that check needs are the designer's to declare. Before this the whole clause came back unparsed, which read as a parse failure when it was a capability gap -- two different things the routing block now tells apart.

performance_criteria.how: performance_check { kind: "lifespan", ... } -- the quantities it needs are the designer's to declare, with sources

routing.structures: organism-design/blueprint.mjs reads the structures named in the text and resolves them to Uberon/CL terms for the taxon; organism_from_blueprint brings the result into the studio
routing.laws: lean_check decides clade scope from the taxon and reports every law as holds / violated / out-of-scope / cannot-evaluate
routing.movement: locomotion_check -- how it moves, which no part list can settle: the scallop theorem, the cycle arithmetic and the Reynolds/Froude regimes
routing.world: ecology_check -- where the clade is recorded, what else is there, and what is recorded eating it. It will not predict exclusion without declared population parameters.

unparsed.reason: organism "fruit fly" has no reference parameter set in this engine (it holds measured parameters for: zebrafish, flying fish, winged zebrafish, wingless flying fish, TFF, the ff-zf chimera). It is not mapped to a "close" one, because the nearest fish is not this animal. A taxon-based design can still be built from it: see spec.taxon, organism_create {taxon} and organism_from_blueprint. The rest of this clause IS parsed: any criterion in it is on the spec, and will be judged once a parameter set for this clade exists.
unparsed.verdict: the organism has no reference parameter set; declare one with organism_create { taxon, declared }

result.scope: A co-design log. Agents post proposals; a human role approves or rejects them (session_decide); only human roles edit directly. Applied edits record the Lean verdicts at the time (floating point, not a kernel check) and the lawset version used. Authors are role labels, not people.
